ostler --full-ids todo add
  Queue an epic, last or first, by its folder name or its slug.
  runs: ostler --full-ids todo add {name} [--front]
  body: AddArgs
  0 → lines of text: the epic is queued, with a warning when it has no epic.md yet
  1 → lines of text: the epic is already in the queue, matched by number or by slug
  carries: AddEpic
    refuses 1 "epic '{canonical}' already in the queue"
      why: adding an epic twice would run it twice, so the queue refuses the second.

ostler --full-ids todo prune
  Drop an epic from the queue.
  runs: ostler --full-ids todo prune {name}
  body: PruneArgs
  0 → lines of text: the queued epic is dropped, named as the queue spelled it
  1 → lines of text: the queue does not hold the epic
  carries: PruneEpic
    refuses 1 "epic '{name}' not in the queue"

ostler --full-ids todo reorder
  Move the named epics to the front of the queue in the order given; the rest keep their order after them. An epic named twice, by the same name or by its number and its slug, is refused.
  runs: ostler --full-ids todo reorder {first} {then}
  body: ReorderArgs
  0 → lines of text: the queue is reordered
  1 → lines of text: the queue does not hold a named epic, and the message lists those it lacks, as typed; or two names stand for the same queued epic, and the message names it as the queue spells it. The queue file is left as it was. A missing epic is refused before a repeat
  carries: ReorderEpics
    refuses 1 'not in queue: {first}, {then}'
    refuses 1 'not in queue: {first}'
    refuses 1 'not in queue: {then}'
    refuses 1 "epic '{repeated}' named more than once"
      why: a repeated name is most often a typo for another epic, so the reorder says which name repeats and writes nothing, where dropping the repeat would reorder the queue on a guess.

ostler --full-ids todo list
  Print the queue, one epic per line, first to last.
  runs: ostler --full-ids todo list
  body: ListArgs
  0 → lines of text: the queued epics, or (none) when the queue is empty
  carries: ListEpics

ostler --full-ids seed add
  List a seed under an epic's Seeds, or replace the one that has the id.
  runs: ostler --full-ids seed add {epic} {seed} --status {status} --layer {layer}
  body: SeedAddArgs
  0 → lines of text: the seed is added, or replaced at the end of the Seeds section
  1 → lines of text: the epic does not exist, or the status or the layer is not one the registry lists
  carries: AddSeed
    refuses 1 "no epic '{epic}'"
    refuses 1 "invalid status '{status}' (one of backlog, researched, covered, resolved, dropped, deferred)"
    refuses 1 "invalid layer '{layer}' (one of frontend, backend, infra)"

ostler --full-ids seed remove
  Take a seed out of an epic's Seeds.
  runs: ostler --full-ids seed remove {epic} {seed}
  body: SeedRemoveArgs
  0 → lines of text: the seed is removed
  1 → lines of text: the epic does not exist, or it lists no seed with the id
  carries: RemoveSeed
    refuses 1 "no epic '{epic}'"
    refuses 1 "no seed '{seed}' in '{epic}'"

ostler --full-ids set-status
  Set a story's status in its frontmatter and in its Implementation Status line. A status that is empty, or made only of spaces and tabs, is refused and no file changes.
  runs: ostler --full-ids set-status {story} {status}
  body: SetStatusArgs
  0 → lines of text: the status is set, written without the spaces and tabs around it
  1 → lines of text: no story has the id, or the status is empty or made only of spaces and tabs; the story file is left as it was
  carries: SetStoryStatus
    refuses 1 "no story with id '{story}'"
    refuses 1 "status of '{story}' cannot be empty"
      why: a script that passes an unset variable would blank the story's status and be told it worked.

ostler --full-ids conflict
  Record the conflict found in a story's acceptance criteria, or clear it.
  runs: ostler --full-ids conflict {story} {text} [--clear]
  body: ConflictArgs
  0 → lines of text: the conflict is recorded or cleared
  1 → lines of text: the text and --clear are both given or both left out, or no story has the id
  carries: RecordConflict
    refuses 1 'pass the conflict text, or --clear — one of the two'
    refuses 1 "no story with id '{story}'"

ostler --full-ids path epic
  Print where an epic lives, relative to the repository.
  runs: ostler --full-ids path epic {name}
  body: PathEpicArgs
  0 → lines of text: the epic's folder, whether or not it exists
  carries: PathOfEpic

sandbox files
  List the watched files of the sandbox with the strings each holds.
  auth: none
  0 → [File]: every watched file with the strings it holds
  carries: ListFiles

GroomTheQueue\nA planner shapes the order the repo works its epics. They list the queue, queue the third epic by its slug, then\n    put it first, move the second ahead of the rest, drop the first, and find where the third epic lives.
WriteSeeds\nA planner lists two seeds under the second epic, rewrites the first with a status and a layer, and takes both\n    out again. The watch reads the epic's page after each step.

TrackAStory
A planner moves the story alpha through its statuses, records a conflict in its criteria, replaces the conflict
    with another, and clears it. They mark it Done with spaces around the word and Blocked: waiting with tabs around it, and the story keeps the words alone.
    A second story keeps its own status throughout.

WrongTurns
A planner slips. They queue an epic twice, prune and reorder epics the queue lacks, name an epic twice in a
    reorder, once by the same name and once by its slug and its number, queue an epic that has no folder yet, list a
    seed with a status and a layer the registry lacks, remove a seed that is not there, give a story an empty status
    or one made of spaces and tabs and then `In progress`, and name a story that does not exist or give a conflict
    no text.
- **first > second**: the queue holds the two epics it starts with. Reached by: a fresh service, nothing done.
- **first > second > third**: the third epic is queued last. Reached by: ostler --full-ids todo add third.
- **third > first > second**: the third epic is queued first. Reached by: ostler --full-ids todo add 0003-third --front.
- **second > first**: the second epic was moved ahead of the first. Reached by: ostler --full-ids todo reorder 0002-second.
- **empty**: both epics were pruned. Reached by: ostler --full-ids todo prune 0001-first; ostler --full-ids todo prune 0002-second.
- **Not started**: the story has not begun. Reached by: a fresh service, nothing done.
- **in-progress**: the story is in progress. Reached by: ostler --full-ids set-status TST-01M585P7WKBH9YJ8E6NA73W4S9 in-progress.
- **Blocked: waiting**: the story is blocked. Reached by: ostler --full-ids set-status TST-01M585P7WKBH9YJ8E6NA73W4S9 'Blocked: waiting'.
- **Done**: the story is done. Reached by: ostler --full-ids set-status TST-01M585P7WKBH9YJ8E6NA73W4S9 Done.
- **Not started with conflict**: a conflict is recorded on the story. Reached by: ostler --full-ids conflict TST-01M585P7WKBH9YJ8E6NA73W4S9 'criteria disagree'.

- **in-progress with conflict**: the story is in progress and a conflict is recorded. Reached by: ostler --full-ids set-status TST-01M585P7WKBH9YJ8E6NA73W4S9 in-progress; ostler --full-ids conflict TST-01M585P7WKBH9YJ8E6NA73W4S9 'criteria disagree'.
- **no seeds**: the epic lists no seeds. Reached by: a fresh service, nothing done.
- **SD-3**: the epic lists the seed SD-3. Reached by: ostler --full-ids seed add 0002-second SD-3.
- **SD-3 + SD-4**: the epic lists the seeds SD-3 and SD-4. Reached by: ostler --full-ids seed add 0002-second SD-3; ostler --full-ids seed add 0002-second SD-4 --status researched --layer frontend.
`ostler todo reorder` refuses a list that names the same queued epic more than once. The refusal prints
`epic '<epic>' named more than once` on standard output, exits 1 and writes no file. `<epic>` is the epic as the
queue spells it, as `todo add` names the epic it finds already queued. It lives in `ostler/ostler/todo.py::reorder`,
which the command line and `Ostler.todo_reorder` share, so both refuse alike.
Two names stand for the same epic when they resolve to the same queue entry, the full name and the short handle
among them. `second` and `0002-second` are a repeat.
The unknown-name refusal runs first and keeps its own message, `not in queue: <names>`. A list that names an epic the
queue lacks, twice or not, is refused for that reason.
A repeated name is refused and not dropped silently. The queue holds an epic once, and `todo add` already refuses a
second copy. A repeat is most often a typo for another epic, so dropping it would reorder the queue on a guess and
tell the operator it worked. A refusal names the repeated epic and lets them type the list they meant. This overturns
the earlier behaviour recorded as entry 1 of `DISAGREEMENTS.md`, which wrote the epic into the queue twice.
The book plays the refusal with the same name twice, with a slug and its number, with a number and its slug, with an
epic the queue lacks twice and with an epic that is queued in some scenes and not in others. The book names two
positions, so a repeat further down a longer list is checked by the story's QA.
A queue file that already holds a repeat is not repaired.
`ostler set-status` refuses a status that is empty or made only of spaces and tabs. The refusal prints
`status of '<story>' cannot be empty` on standard output, exits 1 and writes no file. It lives in
`ostler/ostler/crud.py::set_status`, which the command line and `Ostler.set_status` share, so both refuse alike.
The story lookup runs first. An unknown story keeps its own refusal, `no story with id '<story>'`, whatever the status.
Every other text stays accepted, `Done` and `Blocked: waiting` among them, because the repository names no list of
story statuses. The spaces and tabs around a status are dropped before it is written, and the success line prints
the status without them. Whether a fixed list of statuses should exist stays open, as entry 1 of
`UNDERSPECIFIED.md`.
The book plays the refusal with an empty status, a status of spaces and a status of a tab, each on a known story and
the empty one on an unknown story, and it watches both the frontmatter line and the Implementation Status line so a
refused call is judged to change neither. `Ostler(root).set_status(story, "")` answers a failed result with the same
message; the book reaches the tool through the command line only, so the API half is checked by the story's QA.
A bare slug of an epic that exists on disk (`second`) resolves to its numbered directory (`0002-second`) in
`todo add`, `todo prune`, `todo reorder` and `path epic`. A name with no folder stays as typed, and `todo add`
queues it with a warning that epic selection will skip it. The queue record therefore keeps canonical names, and
the fixtures carry a `canonical` property so a rule's message prints the name the tool prints.
